description: Polyphonic virtual-analogue synthesizer: two oscillators with a sub, ring modulator and noise, two filters and an amp, with any of 22 modulation sources able to reach any of 50 destinations

inputs.text: The note pitch, one volt per octave; its channel count sets the polyphony of the whole synthesizer, and with no cable here the synthesizer produces nothing at all
A modulation source of your own, available to every destination through its assign button
A rise here restarts both envelopes without the gate having to fall first
Audio from outside, which joins the mixer as a sixth source

outputs.text: Carries whatever modulation has been built for it, so a source and depth set here can be sent to another module
The left channel of the synthesizer, or the whole signal when it is the only cable
The right channel of the synthesizer

notes: with no cable in the V/Oct input the whole synthesizer is switched off and both audio outputs rest at 0V, however else it is set
a new instance makes no sound until modulations are assigned: the maker's starting point is V/Oct to both semitone knobs at full, and an envelope or the gate to amp volume at full
a knob with a ring around it can be modulated; a green ring is its base value and a blue ring the depth of the source being assigned, and a lamp under the knob lights when anything modulates it
hovering an assign button lists every destination that source reaches, and hovering a knob lists every source that reaches it; the right-click menu of either can clear those assignments
while an assign button is lit, Rack's own initialise and randomise act only on that source's assignments rather than on the base values
menu: Audio oversampling rate: 1x (low CPU) to 16x (best quality) — runs the oscillators and filters above the sample rate to cut aliasing
Modulation sample rate reduction: 1x (best quality) to 16x (low CPU) — runs the modulation at a fraction of the sample rate, which costs much less processor time
UI sample rate reduction: 1x (best quality) to 64x (low CPU) — sets how often the panel's rings and lamps are worked out
Lock quality settings — keeps the three rate settings where they are when a preset is loaded
Filter ODE Solver — chooses how the filters' differential equations are solved, from a cheap Euler step to fourth-order Runge-Kutta
Filter integrator type — chooses where the non-linearity is placed in each filter integrator

inputs.2:
